messages:
alex_dev: heads up — saw the rust-sdk sampleapp blow up into 100-request bursts right after token refresh, then a bunch of 429s and a long quiet period. anyone seen this pattern?
rita_de: can you paste repro steps + logs? sounds like either backoff/jitter bug or a refresh lock.
alex_dev: steps: run sampleapp against staging with prefetch=4 and concurrent=16, then force token expiry (rotate key). observed seq: token refresh starts, requests queue up ~5s, then a flood when lock releases. log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-22T14:12:33Z] req:id=abc status=401 reason=token_expired
[2026-03-22T14:12:33Z] token: refresh-start
[2026-03-22T14:12:38Z] token: refresh-done
[2026-03-22T14:12:38Z] req:id=abc retry-after=0 -> retry
[2026-03-22T14:12:38Z] req:id=def retry-after=0 -> retry
[2026-03-22T14:12:38Z] many requests -> 429
```
The rust SDK holds an async Mutex across the whole client when refreshing. that looks like a head-of-line blocking issue + our local prefetcher spawns immediate retries.
sam_sdk: yup — i dug in. rust SDK backoff implementation resets per-request backoff state on token refresh completion. combined with prefetcher spawning N immediate attempts you get synchronized retries. The go/js sdks do a non-blocking refresh: they let existing requests wait on a small future and then continue without serializing the entire request pipeline.
maria_onboard: also the sampleapp prefetcher will eagerly pull next pages as soon as a slot frees; with the mutex it means all those prefetch workers are paused and then wake at once. i think two problems: (1) mutex scope too big for refresh and (2) prefetcher should stagger retries after transient auth errors.
rita_de: can you show the code where the mutex is held?
alex_dev: snippet from client.rs — simplified: 
```
async fn ensure_token(&self) {
  let _guard = self.refresh_lock.lock().await; // <-- holds across all requests
  if token_expired() { self.refresh().await; }
}

async fn send(req) {
  self.ensure_token().await;
  transport.send(req).await
}
```
moving the minimal check under the lock and doing refresh only for the single task that wins should fix it.
sam_sdk: propose patch: (a) change ensure_token so only a fast path check is outside the lock, then acquire lock and re-check, (b) add randomized retry jitter for prefetcher, default 50-200ms, (c) honor Retry-After header if > 0 and fold into jitter. i'll open PR.
dave_infra: does this affect hosted users? could cause large request spikes and throttle lots of small customers. we should hotfix sampleapp and ship SDK patch in next minor.
opsbot: deploy-bot: PR #4823 merged to rust-sdk main (https://github.com/redwood-inference/rust-sdk/pull/4823) — CI passed, staging deploy scheduled for 2026-03-23 02:00 UTC. :rocket:
rita_de: nice. can someone open a follow-up ticket to ensure parity across sdks (go/js/python) for token refresh semantics? i can own tracking.
dave_infra: i'll run a quick load test after staging deploy to validate spike smoothing.
alex_dev: thanks all — patch looks good. after deploy i still want a short doc on "safe prefetch" config for our sample apps so new users don't hit this by default.
maria_onboard: i'll add a note to the onboarding guide and include default prefetch jitter values. :thumbsup:
